S1 disabled (engine=strategy2.py). 2026-08-17 session: NO PARAMETER CHANGES. Every S2 constant is owner-locked and the closed record is still n=11. Work went into ONE measurement that changes how the record should be read.
MEASUREMENT ADDED (analyze.py): EXCURSION (MFE/MAE) per trade, in R. peak_roe_pct and max_adverse_pct were already being written to state.json for every trade and NOTHING had ever read them. Win rate and realised R only describe what the EXIT did, so 'should the trail be tighter' was being argued from the trail's own output. MFE describes what the ENTRY offered before any exit rule touched it, which is the only way to tell an entry problem from an exit problem.
WHAT IT SHOWS (n=10 trades carrying excursion data): median MFE +0.80R. 10/10 trades reached +0.5R favourable, but only 2/10 reached +1.0R and 1/10 reached +2.5R. The stop sits at -1.0R. So the typical trade offers 0.8R of profit against 1.0R of risk BEFORE any exit rule is applied. That is a negative-expectancy entry under EVERY possible exit rule, and no trail setting can repair it.
COROLLARY -- the trail is not the culprit. Live TRAIL_START_R=2.5 armed in 1 of 10 trades (10%). A mechanism that engages a tenth of the time cannot be what is costing the money, and tightening it is not the fix the meanR split appears to suggest.
EXIT-REGIME SPLIT (new, previously pooled): strategy2.py last changed 2026-08-05 (TP_R 3.0->5.0, TRAIL_START_R->2.50). Pre-08-05 n=5 WR 60% meanR +0.156; 08-05 onward n=5 WR 20% meanR -0.322. The headline n=11 blends two different exit configurations and should not be quoted as one system. Note the three old-regime 'winners' realised +0.71/+0.98/+0.99R against MFE of +0.73/+1.00/+0.98R -- the old tight ratchet was capturing ~100% of a small excursion, not catching real moves.
FEED-QUALITY JOIN (new): closed trades joined to their own coin's frozen-bar rate. Clean-feed coins (<3% frozen: AVAX 0.4%, ETH 1.2%) n=4 meanR +0.894; dirty-feed coins (>=3%: ARB 12.8%, OP 13.9%, INJ 5.6%) n=3 meanR -1.015. Perfect separation, but n=7 and post-hoc -- an accumulator, not a verdict.
GATE CONTAMINATION CHECK (new, and it came back CLEAN): the worry was that frozen bars manufacture the oversold+ranging combination the gate looks for. Measured: 0 of 242 frozen bars produced a qualifying reading, against 16 of 2775 live bars (0.58%). A frozen price cannot print a NEW extreme, so staleness SUPPRESSES signals rather than faking them. This closes a hypothesis rather than opening one, and it means no staleness guard belongs on the entry path -- it would block nothing.
FOR KAMRAN (locked, not touched, ranked by what the excursion data actually implicates):
  1. TP_R=5.0 and TRAIL_START_R=2.5 are both far outside the strategy's own excursion distribution. TP_R has never filled and the trail arms 10% of the time. Whatever the right values are, they are not these.
  2. The real question is SL_ATR_MULT=1.5 versus the reversion size. Median MFE 0.80R means the reversion move is consistently SMALLER than the stop distance. Either the stop is too wide for the move being harvested, or the entry is too early. This is the one worth re-deriving first.
  3. Do NOT read a 0.5R take-profit off the MFE column, however good it looks (it retrofits to roughly +3.5R over the same 10 trades). Every trade 'would have' hit any target below its own peak, by construction; MFE is sampled at poll frequency; and 1:0.5 RR needs 67% WR with a tail that one gap-through-stop erases.
  4. Direction: 11 of 11 closed trades were LONG, 0 SHORT, against a ~72/28 structural baseline (p~2.4%). The gate census shows why -- shorts are admitted at 6.5% vs 12.1% for longs. This is a long-only dip-buying book in a falling window, which is the single most plausible non-noise explanation for WR 36%.
AVAILABILITY: clean. 98 candles logged 08-12..08-17, every gap explained by quiet hours (02-04). 57 cycle errors on 08-13 were transient upstream 502s, retried at the executor layer (250 retry warnings) and deduplicated before reaching Telegram. No unexplained downtime, no watchdog trips.
